messages:
erin: Quick sync 1: we need a final approach for publishing the JS SDK that plays nice with Node (CJS/ESM), Edge runtimes, and TypeScript. Onboarding bugs piling up in the Vercel/Cloudflare samples.

ben: Repro in Vercel edge sample: import from root pulls CJS in some deploys -> runtime error: "http.Agent is not defined".

maya: yep. Our CJS build depends on node-only http.Agent and axios. Edge builds must use fetch and AbortSignal.

raul: I experimented with conditional exports but learned npm conditions are limited. Example I tried locally (for discussion): 
`exports: { ".": { "require": "./dist/node/index.cjs", "import": "./dist/node/index.mjs", "browser": "./dist/edge/index.mjs" }, "./edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs" }`
But bundlers differ on "browser" and some ignore it.

erin: so consensus leaning to an explicit subpath for edge (`@redwood/sdk/edge`) plus normal root package for node. Less magic and more predictable for users.

sam: I support explicit subpath. Also propose a CI canary publish that installs into our sample apps (Vercel + CF) as part of PR validation. That will catch regressions fast.

ben: Typescript note: TS only respects the top-level "types" field. We should emit a single umbrella d.ts (dist/index.d.ts) that re-exports platform-safe types. Avoid conditional types in package.json.

maya: Implementation parity: keep identical retry/backoff defaults and error shapes across node/edge. Internals can use axios+agent in CJS and fetch+manual backoff in edge. Also add AbortSignal plumbing in both.

raul: DX suggestion: add a runtime guard that detects worker environments and logs a clear error if a CJS build (node-only) was loaded in edge. E.g., check for `typeof process === 'undefined' || !process.versions?.node` and throw a helpful message pointing to `/edge` import.

erin: good. Action items:
- sam: implement canary publish + smoke tests for Vercel and Cloudflare samples
- maya + ben: split auth layers and implement fetch-based edge auth while keeping public retry API identical
- raul: update package.json exports to include explicit `./edge` subpath and verify main/module/browser fields
- devex: update sample READMEs to recommend `@redwood/sdk/edge` for worker deployments and root for node

sam: I'll add a CI job that from PR builds publishes a scoped canary (e.g., `@redwood/sdk-canary`) and runs the sample deployments. Will post status.

ben: small DX bug to fix now: the Vercel README currently says "import createClient from '@redwood/sdk'". Change to `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk/edge'` in edge example and add a note about the root import being node-first.

maya: also add an integration test that asserts error objects have `code`, `status`, and `isRetryable` fields so clients can implement identical retry hooks.

erin: approved. If canary passes, we cut the release next week. Any objections?

raul: :+1:
ben: :+1: will open PR for runtime guard and types bundling
sam: canary CI job opened in #ci, linking in PR
sdk-bot: canary publish job queued by #ci. Will post results. :robot_face:

maya: thanks team. This should reduce onboarding tickets a lot.
erin: great work. We'll follow up on telemetry to see how many users still import root vs /edge.
